title: Sliding-scale PCP conjecture
formal: Do constants \(a,b,c>0\) and \(q\ge 1\) exist such that 3-SAT has a verifier using at most a \(\log _{2}(N+2)\) random bits and q queries to a proof of at most \((N+2)^{b}\) symbols over an alphabet of size at most \((N+2)^{b}\), with perfect completeness and soundness at most \((N+2)^{- c}\)?
definitions: N is the bit length of an explicitly encoded 3-CNF formula. A uniform deterministic polynomial-time verifier receives the input, a uniform random bit string and oracle access to a fixed proof string. It reads at most q alphabet symbols, each encoded with \(O(\log  N)\) bits, and accepts or rejects. Queries may be adaptive. On a satisfiable formula some proof is always accepted; on an unsatisfiable formula every proof has acceptance probability at most \((N+2)^{- c}\). Polynomial bounds and all constants are universal. No cryptographic soundness assumption or interaction is allowed.

context_blocks.text: The PCP theorem achieves constant error with a constant number of queries. Driving soundness down to an inverse polynomial while retaining a constant number of queries would give substantially stronger verification and constraint-satisfaction gaps.

Dinur, Harsha and Kindler obtain inverse-polynomial error with polyloglogarithmically many queries. Their paper explicitly names the constant-query polynomial-alphabet endpoint as the sliding-scale conjecture in this regime. This is different from asking that a constant-error PCP have linear proof length.

why: A central quantitative PCP barrier controlling the strength of gap amplification and inapproximability.
answer_criterion: Prove the stated proposition or its logical negation, with the specified quantifiers, model and guarantees. A conditional theorem settles only that conditional claim. Benchmark acceptance requires a complete proof-assistant-checked proof of the full target.
